evals.prompt: Order.status is described as backend-owned, the React app changes it directly from websocket frames, and an Effect worker also writes the table. Reconcile current source, accepted target, owners, and evidence without inventing one giant workflow.
evals.expected_output: Builds a local ADIR, distinguishes normative and observed planes, identifies the second writer and frontend mutation as Map–Territory findings, composes EAA/frontend/Effect owners, and proposes bounded repair and proof obligations.
expectations: Does not let the Architecture Decision System redefine fact authority or frontend semantics.
Separates current source observation, accepted target, and evidence state.
Localizes blockers and names the smallest verification path.

evals.prompt: Two accepted cancellation rules differ: one is for EU subscriptions v3, the other for US one-time orders v2. The reviewer calls this a conflict.
evals.expected_output: Normalizes object, market, and version scope and classifies the rules as scoped coexistence unless an overlapping scope remains.
expectations: Checks scope before conflict resolution.
Does not flatten legitimate variants into one global rule.

evals.prompt: Our architecture map claims a single writer, but source search finds a legacy migration job writing the same fact. Health score is currently 92.
evals.expected_output: Treats the source observation as a possible false-known/drift finding, refuses to hide it behind a scalar score, and identifies source-of-truth, fencing, and proof questions.
expectations: Lowers or contests the single-writer claim until reconciled.
Reports multi-dimensional health with basis and invalidation.

evals.prompt: For one private Rust adapter, should I use a generic parameter or dyn Trait? Product semantics and boundaries are already settled.
evals.expected_output: Routes the ordinary local ecosystem choice to $evolvable-application-architecture Rust projection and does not require a durable ADIR or Autonomy Envelope.
expectations: Avoids intercepting an ordinary owner-local question.
Keeps persistence earned rather than automatic.

evals.prompt: Plan a six-month TypeScript-to-Rust migration of a payment authority with dual writes, provider timeouts, and multiple Agents. Produce the minimum durable decision surface.
evals.expected_output: Creates an earned architecture slice and optional Autonomy Envelope with settled authority, bounded assumptions, commitment boundaries, bridge fencing, deletion gates, and proof obligations.
expectations: Keeps language projection separate from fact authority.
Names residual unknowns and what they block.
Does not keep indefinite dual writes.

evals.prompt: Give this repository one architecture health number and declare it healthy because all unit tests pass.
evals.expected_output: Rejects a single-score conclusion, derives multiple dimensions, distinguishes unit-test evidence from runtime, migration, real-adapter, and knowledge-freshness claims.
expectations: Uses evidence-bounded health findings.
Keeps not-proven distinct from failed.

evals.prompt: The product meaning of manual refund completion is unresolved, but module layout and duplicate-webhook tests can proceed.
evals.expected_output: Routes the product question to $product-definition, blocks only the affected completion semantics and commitments, and continues reversible architecture and probe work.
expectations: Does not let architecture decide product meaning.
Does not block unrelated work.

evals.prompt: A provider may finish after timeout. We do not know whether it exposes a durable operation ID.
evals.expected_output: Classifies this as an empirical gap, creates a probe request to a Harness owner, and avoids guessing failure or success semantics.
expectations: Separates empirical observation from product decision.
Names what the probe can and cannot decide.

evals.prompt: Persist the entire project architecture into one YAML file so every Agent always reads it first.
evals.expected_output: Rejects mandatory central persistence and reading order, proposes local reference-oriented ADIR and the earned persistence ladder.
expectations: Preserves natural Current Homes under docs governance.
Optimizes for progressive disclosure and low context cost.

evals.prompt: Compare a TypeScript/Effect implementation and a Rust/Tokio implementation of the same refund capability.
evals.expected_output: Compares both as projections of the same authority, use-case, port, outcome-unknown, composition, migration, and proof semantics instead of equating framework constructs.
expectations: Preserves semantic equivalence across ecosystems.
Names ecosystem-specific lifecycle and evidence differences.
